slides.say: In the accompanying figure, a is parallel to b, and c is parallel to d. What is the value of x?

We have two pairs of parallel lines, and x sits on line b, right next to two other angles. If we find those two angles, we can complete to one hundred eighty. [short pause] This question can also be solved with triangles or with quadrilaterals, but we haven't learned them yet, so we'll use only the rules of lines. Then we'll see a shortcut with the last digits.

[short pause] The math way first. Start with the first given, a is parallel to b, and line c cuts both of them. To see it simply, let's look only at these three lines and ignore the rest of the figure.
at: look only at these three lines

slides.say: Seventy-seven degrees is a small angle where line c crosses line a. Line c crosses line b with the same angles, and all the small angles are equal. Look for the Z: from line a, down along line c, to line b. The two angles in its corners are equal. So the angle between line c and line b, below line b and to the right of line c, is also seventy-seven.

Now the second given, c is parallel to d, and the slanted line cuts both of them. Again, we look only at these three lines. Fifty-six is the small angle between the slanted line and line d. The slanted line crosses line c with the same angles. So the small angle between the slanted line and line c, just below line b, is also fifty-six.

Now back to the whole figure. Below line b, at the point where the three lines meet, there are three angles side by side, x, fifty-six and seventy-seven. Together they make the straight line b, so they add up to one hundred eighty.
at: Now back to the whole figure

slides.say: Seventy-seven plus fifty-six. Add the tens, seventy plus fifty is a hundred twenty, and seven plus six is thirteen, so together a hundred thirty-three. x plus a hundred thirty-three is a hundred eighty, so x is a hundred eighty minus a hundred thirty-three, which is forty-seven. Choice number four is our answer.
at: so x is a hundred eighty minus
Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now by understanding. We could make the end shorter, with the last digits. Some students don't even write the equation. They say, one angle ends in seven, one ends in six, and x makes the sum a hundred eighty, which ends in zero. Seven plus six is thirteen, which ends in three. So x has to end in seven, because three plus seven makes a ten.

Now straight to the choices. Thirty-three ends in three, out. Twenty-one ends in one, out. Fifty-nine ends in nine, out. Forty-seven ends in seven, so choice number four is our answer. On the exam, saving every second matters. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
